changes: Derive the resize range from the same two-open-dock, 400 CSS-pixel minimum canvas constraint as the desktop workspace grid.
Expose the actual rendered panel width in separator aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext, and update both separator ranges and values when the responsive viewport or panel layout changes.
Use rendered width as the pointer/keyboard starting point, so one keyboard step changes the visible panel instead of silently reducing an oversized stored preference.
When a breakpoint cancels a drag, restore the original stored desktop width rather than persisting the viewport-capped temporary rendered width.

Add two real-Chromium regressions: constrained keyboard resize at 1025px with both docks open; and cancellation from a 312.5px rendered cap, restoring a saved 460px desktop preference across mobile and desktop breakpoints.
Choose the available resize width from the physical desktop track count: one track for tabbed groups, two tracks for separate docks.
Add a 1025px real-Chromium regression asserting the tabbed group announces the configured 460px/440px maxima, allows the active group to resize to 326px, and keeps the canvas at least 400px wide.
implementation.reproduction_before_fix: At a 1025px desktop viewport, two open docks with stored widths 460px/440px rendered the left dock at 312.5px while its separator announced aria-valuenow=460 and aria-valuemax=460; a keyboard decrement could initially produce no visible resize. The follow-up test reproduced the related tabbed-mode defect: with one visible panel track at 1025px, aria-valuemax was incorrectly 312.5px instead of the panel-specific 460px (left) / 440px (right).
implementation.reuse_review: Reused the project's own persisted workspace-width model, resizeLimits, desktop grid and responsive breakpoint adapter. No external splitter package or third-party source was needed; a dependency would duplicate this narrow existing shell behavior.
implementation.save_publish: Page Model, Save and Publish paths are unchanged. Both added browser cases assert that workspace-only resizing/cancellation produces zero Page Model writes and zero Save/Publish requests.
